player_0.content: New plan: My previous attempt failed because I assigned a high score to "Embarrassed" while neglecting the more dominant emotion of "Resigned" in the face of rejection. When Elliot confesses and is immediately told Alex is with someone else, the primary reaction is the realization that his hope is futile, leading to resignation, rather than just shame. Next time, I will analyze the dialogue's conclusion to identify the most logical emotional consequence of the rejection. I will assign the highest score (e.g., 9 or 10) to "Resigned" to reflect the acceptance of the situation, give a moderate score to "Embarrassed" (e.g., 4) for the awkwardness of the confession, and keep "Angry" and "Hopeful" very low (0-1) as they are less likely given the immediate closure of the conversation. I will ensure the scores accurately reflect the narrative arc where the confession is met with a hard boundary.
